Simple mediation

Source: vignettes/articles/model-simple.qmd

One treatment, one mediator, one outcome: the model behind most mediation analyses. This page runs it three ways and reads the result. Part of the Models collection; for a one-page lookup see the Reference Card.

Structure X to M to Y, with the direct path X to Y
Class returned MediationData
Indirect effect \(a \, b\)
Routes med(), fit_mediation(), extract_mediation() on lm/glm, lavaan, or fit_sem() 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
covs <- c("covariate1", "covariate2")

When to use it

Use it when one mediator carries the effect of the treatment and you have no reason to expect a treatment-by-mediator interaction. If the mediator and the outcome interact with the treatment, see interaction; for two or more mediators see serial and parallel.

Route 1: one line

med() fits both models, extracts the structure and returns the result.

res <- med(mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
           outcome = "outcome", covariates = covs)
quick(res)
NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %

Route 2: formulas

fit_mediation() takes one formula per model, so each model can carry its own covariates.

fit <- fit_mediation(
  formula_y = outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  formula_m = mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1"
)
tidy(fit, type = "effects", conf.int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.333    0.0645  0.206       0.459
2 nde      0.206    0.110  -0.00936     0.421
3 te       0.539    0.119   0.304       0.773

Route 3: models you already fitted 

fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
            mediation_demo)
x <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,
                       treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
paths(x)
        a         b   c_prime
0.5826425 0.5711384 0.2057983

The same object comes from a lavaan fit (extract_mediation(lavaan_fit, ...)) or from the native engine (extract_mediation(fit_sem(...), ...)); see Cookbook recipe 10 and recipe 11.

Reading the result

Quantity Call Meaning
a paths(x) effect of the treatment on the mediator
b paths(x) effect of the mediator on the outcome, holding the treatment fixed
c_prime paths(x), nde(x) direct effect of the treatment
NIE nie(x) indirect effect, \(a \, b\)
TE te(x) total effect, NIE plus NDE
PM pm(x) proportion mediated, NIE over TE 
c(nie = unname(nie(x)), nde = unname(nde(x)), te = unname(te(x)),
  pm = unname(pm(x)))
      nie       nde        te        pm
0.3327695 0.2057983 0.5385678 0.6178786

Intervals for the effects come from the delta method (tidy(), confint()). For a bootstrap interval see Bootstrap Inference.

Assumptions and limits

  • The treatment is randomized, or the models adjust for every confounder of the treatment-outcome, treatment-mediator and mediator-outcome relations.
  • The mediator-outcome confounders must be in both models; leaving a covariate out of one biases that path.
  • A near-zero total effect makes the proportion mediated unstable.
  • The default glm engine is maximum likelihood on independent observations; for clustered data see Cookbook recipe 9.
